questiontext.text: In an Activity-On-Edge (AOE) network, what do the edges and vertices represent?

answer.text: Edges are activities with durations; vertices are events (milestones)

feedback.text: Correct — AOE puts activities on edges and events on vertices.

answer.text: Edges are events; vertices are activities

feedback.text: That describes an Activity-On-Vertex (AOV) network, not AOE.

answer.text: Both edges and vertices are activities

feedback.text: No — only the edges carry activities in AOE.

answer.text: Edges have no weights; only vertices are weighted

feedback.text: No — AOE edges carry the activity durations as weights.

generalfeedback.text: An AOE network is a weighted DAG where each edge is an activity with a duration and each vertex is an event marking the completion of incoming activities.

questiontext.text: The critical path in an AOE network is the ______ path from the start event to the finish event.

answer.text: Longest — it equals the minimum project completion time

feedback.text: Correct — the longest path determines the shortest possible completion time.

answer.text: Shortest — it equals the minimum project completion time

feedback.text: No — the critical path is the longest path, not the shortest.

answer.text: Path with the fewest edges

feedback.text: No — edge count is irrelevant; total duration matters.

answer.text: Any path with at least one zero-slack activity

feedback.text: No — the critical path is specifically the longest one.

generalfeedback.text: Because all activities must finish for the project to complete, the longest (critical) path fixes the minimum overall completion time.

questiontext.text: How much slack (allowable delay) does an activity on the critical path have?

answer.text: Zero — delaying it delays the whole project

feedback.text: Correct — critical activities have zero slack.

answer.text: Equal to the activity's duration

feedback.text: No — critical activities cannot be delayed at all.

answer.text: Equal to the project length minus the path length

feedback.text: No — that would be positive; critical activities have zero slack.

answer.text: Always exactly one time unit

feedback.text: No — the slack is exactly zero.

generalfeedback.text: Slack = latest start - earliest start. On the critical path these coincide, so slack is zero and any delay pushes the finish event.

questiontext.text: Which two passes compute the earliest and latest event times used to find the critical path?

answer.text: A forward pass (earliest event time) then a backward pass (latest event time)

feedback.text: Correct — forward for earliest, backward for latest.

answer.text: Two forward passes over the graph

feedback.text: No — the second pass runs backward from the finish event.

answer.text: Dijkstra's algorithm run twice

feedback.text: No — event times use topological forward/backward passes on a DAG.

answer.text: A single BFS from the start event

feedback.text: No — you need both a forward and a backward pass.

generalfeedback.text: Processing vertices in topological order forward gives earliest event times; processing in reverse gives latest event times. Activities whose earliest = latest start are critical.

questiontext.text: An AOE network must be a directed acyclic graph (DAG) for the critical-path method to apply.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct — a cycle would make event times undefined; AOE networks are DAGs.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: It must be acyclic; a cycle prevents well-defined earliest/latest event times.

questiontext.text: An AOE network can have more than one critical path.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct — several longest paths of equal length can coexist.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Multiple paths can tie for the longest length, so critical paths need not be unique.

questiontext.text: The allowable delay of an activity without delaying the project is called its ______ (one English word).

answer.text: slack

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: slack*

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: float

feedback.text: Correct — "float" is an accepted synonym for slack.

questiontext.text: Which statements about the critical path are true? (select all that apply)

answer.text: Its total length equals the minimum project completion time

feedback.text: Yes — the longest path sets the shortest possible finish time.

answer.text: Every activity on it has zero slack

feedback.text: Yes — critical activities cannot be delayed.

answer.text: Shortening any non-critical activity always shortens the project

feedback.text: No — only shortening the critical path (up to a point) shortens the project.

answer.text: It is the path with the smallest total edge weight

feedback.text: No — it is the largest total weight (longest) path.

generalfeedback.text: The critical path is the longest path; its length is the minimum completion time and its activities have zero slack. Speeding up non-critical activities does not help until they too become critical.
